Subject: Transfer-impact addendum — lift-and-shift plan and procurement questions

Hi Emily,

Thanks again for walking through the draft Order Form this morning. I've pulled together the core outstanding items that will determine whether we proceed with the standard DPA + SCCs or require the transfer-impact addendum / additional localization commitments. Short summary and asks below so we can align procurement and legal.

Outstanding technical/legal items that affect commercial uplift:
- Hosting routing: whether traffic must be pinned to an EU region (we flagged options: Hosted EU only vs EU-residency supplement).
- KMS / key ownership: customer-managed keys (HSM/KMS) or Redwood-managed? If customer-managed, we need the KMS vendor and key lifecycle expectations.
- Subprocessor evidence: SOC2 + subprocessor list + willingness to sign export limitations addendum.
- SCCs: confirmation if you require Controller-to-Processor SCCs + Annex II information in the contract.

Proposed mutual action plan (MAP):
1) You confirm KMS requirement and whether VPC peering is required — by Tue 21 Jul.
2) We provide a draft transfer-impact addendum and estimated pricing uplift for EU-only routing — by Thu 22 Jul.
3) Procurement and Legal call (30 min) to finalize SOW/order form and DocuSign timeline — Fri 23 Jul.

I've attached our latest redlines (redlines_v3.docx) and a transfer mapping workbook (transfer-mapping.xlsx) showing how requests map to operation/engineering constraints.

If that MAP looks good I will loop Ben and Karthik to prepare the uplift estimate and evidence packet.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Transfer-impact addendum — lift-and-shift plan and procurement questions

Hi Laura — thanks for the clear breakdown. A few clarifications from our side:

- KMS: We do require customer-managed keys for the EU pilot (HSM-backed preferred). Can you confirm whether Redwood supports bringing our AWS KMS keys or an HSM in front of the service?
- VPC / network: For the initial scope, we expect VPC peering (private endpoints) for all production workloads. Test environments can be multi-region.
- Evidence: Procurement asks for SOC 2 Type II report and a current subprocessor list (with locations) before we can sign.
- SCCs: Legal prefers Controller-to-Processor SCCs and requests Annex II fields populated. If Redwood can provide a short Annex II package we can avoid a protracted review.

Procurement also asked for an initial estimate of any uplift to cover EU-only routing + KMS/HSM support. Can you share numbers or a range? If helpful, I'm available Wed 22 Jul 09:00–12:00 CEST for a short call.

Cheers,
